summary.text: Astronomy is the natural science that studies celestial objects and the events in space, which means everything that originates beyond Earth's atmosphere.
It uses mathematics, physics, and chemistry to explain where planets, stars, galaxies, and comets came from and how they change over time.
It is one of the oldest natural sciences, and amateurs still take an active part, for example by helping to find new comets.

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: Everything that originates beyond Earth's atmosphere

facts.label: Whole-universe branch
facts.value: Cosmology studies the universe as a whole

facts.label: Babylonian eclipse cycle
facts.value: Lunar eclipses recur every saros, 223 synodic months

facts.label: Meaning of the name
facts.value: Greek for the study of stars, by 'star' and 'law'

items.prompt: A friend says reading a horoscope is the same thing as doing astronomy. What is the real difference between the two?

options.label: Astronomy covers only planets, while astrology covers only stars
Astronomy is supported by physics, while astrology is not
They have unrelated origins, and only astrology uses mathematics
Astronomy says human affairs follow the sky, astrology only measures it

items.explain: The two fields share a common origin but became distinct, with astronomy supported by physics. Astrology is the belief that human affairs are tied to the positions of celestial objects.

items.prompt: A farming community thousands of years ago watches the sky closely. What practical need mainly drove early astronomy like theirs?

options.label: Predicting the outcome of wars between cities
Proving that the Earth moves around the Sun
Measuring how far away other galaxies lie
Keeping calendars that guide planting and harvest

items.explain: The early development of astronomy was driven by practical needs such as agricultural calendars.

items.prompt: A medieval scholar uses a model with the Earth at the center and the Sun circling it. It matches the sky better than any rival model on offer. How should we describe that model?

options.label: It was later discredited, yet it was the most accurate then available
It was always wrong, so scholars quickly ignored it
It was confirmed as correct and still stands today
It fit observations worse than the alternatives

items.explain: The Earth-centered Ptolemaic system was eventually discredited, but it gave the most accurate predictions for the positions of astronomical bodies available at that time.

items.prompt: In the 3rd century BC a Greek thinker suggests that the Earth and the planets travel around the Sun. What is this kind of model now called?

options.label: Geocentric
Ptolemaic
Heliocentric
Saros

items.explain: Aristarchus of Samos proposed a Solar System with the Earth and planets going around the Sun, now called the heliocentric model. The geocentric model of Ptolemy put the Earth at the center instead.

items.prompt: You buy a backyard telescope and sweep the sky hoping to find something new. In which kind of discovery have amateurs actually helped?

options.label: Designing the instruments used in space observatories
Working out the cycle of lunar eclipses
Building early analog computers for the heavens
Spotting new icy visitors that trail a bright tail

items.explain: Amateur astronomers have helped with many important discoveries, such as finding new comets, especially of transient events.

items.prompt: A university research team of professional astronomers all hold physics degrees, and they call their work astrophysics. Is that a contradiction?

options.label: Yes, because astrophysics only studies Earth's atmosphere
No, in modern use the two terms are often used interchangeably
Yes, because astronomy forbids the use of physics
No, because astrophysics is simply the older name for it

items.explain: Many professional astronomers have physics rather than astronomy degrees, and in modern use the two terms are often interchangeable.
